label: judge: reports
result: SR1–SR24 are written to `/Users/workingmyassof/satbank/spec/v2-upgrades/reports.md` (about 138 KB) and are not committed. The file has all four parts: a 36-row scorecard against TopTierPrep, 24 accepted upgrades merged from all three designers' 35 proposals and 53 parity gaps, spec overrides with line numbers, and a Rejected list. The upgrades that make it "way better" rather than parity: every miss priced in points by re-scoring the sitting, split by cause and by difficulty, including the easier-Module-2 route cap (SR1). A path to the target ("4 questions from 700"), a Fix ordered by points per minute, and a What-if mode (SR2). A Second look, where students re-answer their misses before the key shows, which separates slips from gaps and fixes the spec's conflict with R21 (SR3). A report that updates as fixes are proven, with a Prove-it test (SR6). Slot-by-slot comparison of a twin, rematch or any two sittings, using Tests' twin kind in place of the spec's duplicate `{like}` (SR7). A cause on every miss that the student can correct in one tap (SR8). The confidence, flags and time-away region that Tests §3.4.7 promised but §3.5 never designed (SR9). Crowd data and levels L1–L7 on every question (SR12). A clock replay of each module against per-question time budgets (SR13). Two more fix things: SR5 puts the band on College Board's published national percentiles, because with 12 finished mocks the in-site percentile would read "needs 20" for months, and it needs the real table typed in with its source and year before it can ship. SR12 regroups the challenge crowd by named misconception, because twin challenges (decision 1) mean option letters never line up. Wherever a sibling file already specifies a function (for example T7's causes, T16's re-scoring, P1's steps, U3's instant check), the upgrades call it instead of redefining it. The changes they need in Part 2 and in the Today, Practice, Shell, Tests, Plan, Review and Compete specs are in the "Outside the section" table. Nothing adds a table or a column. Rejected items include O4's guided stepper, which hides the report behind screens (decision 4), a second family taxonomy duplicating U6, per-skill and cohort percentiles, a template versioning system, and a practice-only score.
